name: Particle senses
description: What each particle can mean, and the cues that favour one reading over another. Senses are shown to the learner whether or not a cue fires; ranking is an addition, never a filter.

particles.note: The one learners most often stall on, and the only common particle whose spelling is also an inflected form of something else: 静かで is the て-form of だ, not で at all.

senses.label: not で at all — the て-form of だ
senses.gloss: This is だ joining onto the next clause, the way て joins verbs: 静かで、きれいだ is "it is quiet, and it is pretty". Nothing is being marked here.

examples.japanese: 音楽が好きで、毎日聴いています。
examples.english: I like music, and I listen to it every day.

examples.japanese: 私は舞踏家が職業で、ジャズダンスを教えています。
examples.english: I am a dancer by trade and I teach jazz dance.

senses.label: where the action happens
senses.gloss: The place an action is carried out. 図書館で勉強する — the studying happens at the library. Contrast に, which marks where something ends up or simply is.

examples.japanese: 台所でお母さんの手伝いをしていたの。
examples.english: I helped my mother in the kitchen.

examples.japanese: この公園でローラースケートをしてもいいですか。
examples.english: Can we roller-skate in this park?

senses.label: what it is done with
senses.gloss: The tool, vehicle or method used. 電車で行く — by train. ペンで書く — with a pen.

examples.japanese: 歩いて行きますか？それともバスで行きますか？
examples.english: Will you go on foot or by bus?

examples.japanese: 私は貴方が汽車で行くことを勧めます。
examples.english: I recommend you to go by train.

senses.label: what it is made of
senses.gloss: The material something is made from. 木で作る — made out of wood.

examples.japanese: この机は堅い材質の木でできている。
examples.english: This desk is made of hard wood.

examples.japanese: その小さな像は純金でできていると言われている。
examples.english: The small statue is said to be made of fine gold.

senses.label: because of it
senses.gloss: The cause or reason. 病気で休む — off because of illness. Usually an event or a state rather than a thing.

examples.japanese: 彼女は風邪でダウンした。
examples.english: She came down with a cold.

examples.japanese: その建物の一部分だけが地震で破壊された。
examples.english: Only part of the building has been destroyed by the earthquake.

senses.label: within that much
senses.gloss: The amount, time or scope something happens inside. 三日で終わる — finished within three days. 日本で一番 — the most in Japan.

examples.japanese: チケットは一週間で完売した。
examples.english: The tickets sold out within a week.

examples.japanese: あと１０分で手が空く。
examples.english: I will be free in ten minutes.

particles.note: Almost always the direct object. The two exceptions are worth knowing because they look wrong otherwise: a place can take を when it is left or passed through.

senses.label: what the action is done to
senses.gloss: The direct object. 本を読む — reading a book. This is what を is doing unless the verb is one of movement.

examples.japanese: ジェーン自身がこの手紙を書いた。
examples.english: Jane wrote the letter herself.

examples.japanese: 先週の日曜日におかしな映画を見た。
examples.english: We saw a funny movie last Sunday.

senses.label: the place being left
senses.gloss: With verbs of leaving, を marks what is departed from rather than what is acted on. 家を出る — leaving the house. 電車を降りる — getting off the train.
dictionary: indicates point of departure or separation of action

examples.japanese: ６時起床、７時家を出る。
examples.english: Got up at six, and left home at seven.

examples.japanese: 島を出る手だてはありません。
examples.english: There's no way off the island.

senses.label: the route travelled
senses.gloss: With verbs of motion, を marks the ground covered. 公園を歩く — walking through the park. 橋を渡る — crossing the bridge.

examples.japanese: 私たちは並木道を歩いた。
examples.english: We walked along an avenue lined with trees.

examples.japanese: ワシが空を飛んでいる。
examples.english: An eagle is flying in the sky.

particles.note: The widest of the five. Most of its readings are separated by the verb rather than by the noun.

senses.label: where something is
senses.gloss: With いる and ある, に marks where a thing simply is. 部屋にいる — being in the room. Contrast で, which marks where something is *done*.

examples.japanese: 机の上に本があります。
examples.english: There is a book on the desk.

examples.japanese: この市にはいくつもの映画館がある。
examples.english: There are many movie theaters in this city.

senses.label: where it ends up
senses.gloss: The place something moves to. 学校に行く — going to school. Interchangeable with へ here, though へ stresses the direction rather than the arrival.

examples.japanese: 生徒達はみんな家に帰りました。
examples.english: All the students have gone home.

examples.japanese: ヘレンは昨年日本に来た。
examples.english: Helen came to Japan last year.

senses.label: when it happens
senses.gloss: A point in time. 三時に会う — meeting at three. Used with clock times and dates, not with 今日 or 明日.

examples.japanese: 彼は６月にオランダから帰国しました。
examples.english: He returned from Holland in June.

examples.japanese: スピーチコンテストは１１月９日に行われた。
examples.english: The speech contest took place on the ninth of November.

senses.label: who receives it
senses.gloss: The person something is given, told or shown to. 友達に話す — telling a friend.

examples.japanese: 君にこのペンダントをあげるよ。
examples.english: I'll give you this pendant.

examples.japanese: 私たちは父にバースデイプレゼントをあげるつもりです。
examples.english: We will give Father a birthday present.

senses.label: what it is for
senses.gloss: With a verb stem before it and a motion verb after, に marks the errand. 買い物に行く — going shopping.

examples.japanese: 映画を見に行きませんか。
examples.english: How about going to the movies?

examples.japanese: ちょっとそこまでコーヒーを飲みに行く。
examples.english: Come round the corner for coffee.

senses.label: making an adverb
senses.gloss: After words like 本当, 一緒 and 絶対, に turns the word into an adverb: 本当に really, 一緒に together, 絶対に absolutely. It marks no place, time or receiver here.

examples.japanese: 本当に美味しい。
examples.english: It tastes really yummy.

examples.japanese: 一緒に行きます。
examples.english: I'm coming with you.

particles.note: The class worth learning is the second one: a set of predicates that take が where English would use an object, which is why 日本語が分かる is not a mistake.

senses.label: who or what does it
senses.gloss: The subject, picked out as new information or as the specific one. 誰が来た？ — who came?
dictionary: indicates the subject of a sentence

examples.japanese: まもなく雨が降りそうだ。
examples.english: It is going to rain soon.

examples.japanese: 家へついたら電話が鳴っていた。
examples.english: The telephone was ringing when I got home.

senses.label: what is liked, wanted or understood
senses.gloss: A group of predicates take が where English takes an object: 好き, 嫌い, 上手, ほしい, できる, 分かる, 見える, 聞こえる. 日本語が分かる — I understand Japanese. Nothing is being marked as the doer here.

examples.japanese: 欠点があるけどやはり彼が好きです。
examples.english: I love him despite his faults.

examples.japanese: 画像のアップロードの仕方が分かりません。
examples.english: I can't figure out how to upload an image.

particles.note: は against が is information structure, not word meaning — which is why the cues here are thin and this mostly shows the readings rather than choosing between them.

senses.label: what the sentence is about
senses.gloss: Sets the topic — everything after it is a comment on this. 私は学生です — as for me, student. It does not mark the subject; it says what is being discussed.

examples.japanese: 私の父は会社員です。
examples.english: My father is an office worker.

examples.japanese: 日本は世界のハイテク産業のリーダーだ。
examples.english: Japan is a leader in the world's high-tech industry.

senses.label: this one, as against others
senses.gloss: Singles something out against alternatives. コーヒーは飲みます — coffee I do drink (implying something else I do not). A second は in the same sentence is usually this.
dictionary: indicates contrast with another option (stated or unstated)

examples.japanese: 私たちはボストンまでは行きませんでした。
examples.english: We didn't go as far as Boston.

examples.japanese: 「コーヒーのお替わりいる？」「うん、ぼくのは少なめ、弟のには多めについでね」
examples.english: "Do you want another cup of coffee?" "Sure, make mine on the small side but be generous with my brother's."
